newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Lacklustre Australian stocks limp to flat finish.
newsitem.headline: Lacklustre Australian stocks limp to flat finish.

text.p: A lacklustre Australian share market limped to a flat finish on Thursday with a bullish streak on Wall Street ignored in favour of a wary eye on the upcoming local profit season.
The All Ordinaries index inched up 0.1 points to 2,735.1, swinging around square all day and but never venturing more than eight points either way.
Brokers said the market seemed content to churn near the top of its record breaking 1997 range.
"There has been a slowdown in the order flow a bit and I suppose that's because the market is where it is," said Eric Gale, director of institutions at investment bank Ord Minnett.
"It is still holding the high ground pretty much, it's not too far from an absolute top, but people are struggling to find value (at these levels)."
After yesterday's interest rate reduction, the next key influence was likely to be the flood of June 30 profit reports washing through the market over the next six weeks.
Some concerns still lingered about expectations from this data with traders suggesting some caution was appropriate.
"I hope the market is not demanding more than is possible, in some cases I think they may be," said Gale, a sentiment echoed by others.

"People are getting a little bit concerned about just what our reporting season is going to bring, notwithstanding the decrease in interest rates yesterday," said Peake Lands Kirwan broker Kevin Lourey.

Among individual stocks, slot machine maker Aristocrat Leisure relisted after a week-long suspension 311813 and plunged 37 cents to A$2.50 (US$1.85) before recovering to close 22 cents down at A$2.65 amid concerns over its Colorado licence renewal refusal.

Also on the downside, grocery retailer and wholesaler Davids Ltd dived 15 cents to a record low of 85 cents before climbing back some way to close down 12 cents at 88 cents in active trade with 2.5 million shares traded.
The company yesterday announced a A$262 million writedown and restructured senior management. Since hitting a 1997 high of A$1.82, Davids shares have halved in value.
Among a generally lacklustre gold sector, Plutonic Resources pulled ahead, adding nearly five percent to A$3.98 as investors, impressed by its quarterly report, bought in.
"Record production, cash costs coming down, it was a great quarterly," said dealer Justin Hondris, of Hartley Poynton.

Elsewhere, Amalgamated Holdings, owner of the Thredbo ski village, the scene of a landslide overnight under which 20 people are thought to be trapped, ended 20 cents down at A$6.90, although traders were sceptical of the connection given the nature of the day's patchy trade and the paucity of activity in the stock.
"It is a thin stock at the best of times," said one dealer.
Rises slightly shaded falls, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
